description: Bevy game engine (Rust) targeting the browser via WebAssembly. Ships a minimal DefaultPlugins app — camera + 3D cube + rotation system — plus a Trunk.toml so `trunk serve` builds WASM, runs wasm-bindgen, and hosts the page in one command. Foundation for Bevy web games, interactive demos, and Rust-first 3D content.

buildHints.whenToUse: Rust-first game or interactive 3D content that needs to run in a browser. Bevy gives you an ECS, rendering, input, audio, and a plugin ecosystem; Trunk handles the WASM build + asset pipeline. Pick wasm-rust instead if you only need a pure compute module with no engine.
firstSteps: Install the toolchain once: `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown` then `cargo install --locked trunk wasm-bindgen-cli`. Trunk is the standard Bevy-web build tool — it wraps wasm-bindgen + wasm-opt and serves the page.
Run: `trunk serve` — it compiles Rust to WASM, runs wasm-bindgen, writes `dist/`, and opens http://localhost:8080 with hot-reload on Rust changes.

Edit `src/main.rs` — the Bevy app adds DefaultPlugins, spawns a camera + light + rotating cube, and registers a system that rotates it. Replace the cube with your geometry and add systems/resources as the game grows.
Ship: `trunk build --release` emits `dist/` with a hashed WASM bundle, JS shim, and HTML; deploy to any static host.

For audio + advanced renderer features, enable the right Bevy features in Cargo.toml (`bevy = { version = "0.14", features = ["default"] }`); strip defaults for a smaller bundle when you only need 2D.
gotchas: Bevy requires the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target AND wasm-bindgen at the exact version pinned in Cargo.lock — drift gives cryptic `imported memory` link errors. Always install with `--locked`.

WebGPU backend is Chrome/Edge 113+ and Safari 18+ stable; on Firefox (stable) Bevy falls back to WebGL2. If you depend on a WebGPU-only feature (compute shaders, bindless resources), guard it and expose a fallback or gate the app.
Asset loading uses fetch() relative to the page — `bevy::asset::AssetServer` expects files under the Trunk `public_url` (set in Trunk.toml). Dropping assets next to src/ will 404.
Bevy's WASM binary is large even for small apps (~10–20 MB debug, ~3–6 MB release with wasm-opt). Always ship release builds with `wasm-opt -Oz` (Trunk does this by default).
The default Bevy logger uses ANSI escape codes — on the browser console they render as garbage. Swap in `bevy::log::LogPlugin` with `level: Level::INFO` and a custom filter for clean WASM logs.
Bevy 0.14 removed some 0.13 re-exports; if you're porting an older example, check the migration guide — API churn is real between minor versions.
architectureNotes: One `App::new()` per process — Bevy is not reentrant. All plugins, systems, and resources attach to that single app.
Systems are stateless functions operating on queries + resources; do not hold handles across frames in locals. State belongs in `Resource`s or `Component`s.
Keep WASM-specific code under `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]` so the same crate still runs natively for fast iteration.
